name: Axiom Systems Distributed Identity Cloak DIC-2
product_name: Axiom Systems Distributed Identity Cloak DIC-2
description: A device that floods local surveillance systems with dozens of false identity signals, making it impossible to determine the wearer's true identity among a crowd of spoofed personas. The DIC-2 broadcasts multiple simultaneous false biometric, neural interface, and Diaspora identity signatures within a 10-meter radius, creating a cloud of phantom identities that overwhelms facial recognition, biometric tracking, and identity correlation systems. Within the cloud, every person appears to be everyone else — faces do not match IDs, neural signatures do not match bodies, and tracking systems lose the ability to associate any specific identity with a specific physical person.

specifications.info: biometric tracking; neural interface correlation; Diaspora identity; instant effect

story_hooks: A DIC-2 was activated in a crowded transit hub, causing every surveillance system in the area to simultaneously flag 300 identity mismatches — in the confusion, someone walked through security with a weapon that would normally have been detected through identity correlation.

A permanent DIC-2 installation has been discovered in a Tier 3 building, creating an always-on identity fog that makes the building's occupants effectively untrackable — the building has become a haven for anyone who needs to disappear.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular module resembling a reinforced access card or slim tactical pouch. Pentagonal cross-section with beveled edges, designed to break up visual silhouette. Deliberately unmarked and generic-looking to avoid drawing attention.
physical_description.dimensions: 12cm × 8cm × 2.5cm (roughly the size of a thick wallet or small ammunition magazine)
physical_description.weight_description: 250 grams — light enough for pocket carry or belt loop attachment; does not create noticeable weight distribution
physical_description.primary_material: Matte-finished titanium alloy composite housing with rubberized polymer grip zones
physical_description.finish: Satin-textured, non-reflective surface. Intentionally dull to avoid glint or visual detection. Slight industrial wear consistent with daily carry.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal grey primary with faded burnt sienna accent strips along seams (Diaspora heritage aesthetic). No bright indicators.
physical_description.interface_elements: Single recessed physical button (momentary contact) on edge. Minimal haptic feedback. No visible display — all activation feedback is subtle vibration or low-frequency tone through bone conduction.
distinctive_features: Micro-antenna array visible as faint etched grid pattern across top surface
Heat-dissipation venting along edges (device runs warm during broadcast)
Faded regulatory stamps: AXIOM SYSTEMS logo, Φ pricing tier marker (Tier 4+), FCC/GLMZ compliance markings
Subtle LED indicator beneath frosted plastic window — appears dark when inactive, faint amber during broadcast
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: AXIOM SYSTEMS embossed on lower left corner (almost worn smooth). Batch code and holographic authenticity sticker on rear. No other branding — deliberate anonymity.
physical_description.condition_typical: User's version shows minor scratches from pocket carry, slight patina on edges. Battery indicator micro-screen (hidden under rubberized strip) glows faintly when active. Device feels warm to touch during 10-meter radius broadcast.

Device lit by cool blue-green neon strip light casting sharp shadows. Nearby: a portable biometric scanner displaying 30 conflicting face signatures on its screen.
